brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Hex base pieces at (0,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1) at level 0, plus a North half base at (1,1) that carries the drawer. Joint bolts at (0,0)-(1,0), (0,0)-(0,1) and (0,-1)-(0,0) lock the base bodies together; check_build shows no LOOSE_BODY warning.
Three drop-in bins: 'Bin, full depth, 3 compartments' at (0,0) and (0,-1), and 'Bin, full depth, 2 compartments' at (1,0). They hang on their rims and can be lifted out.
One drawer (drawer:0#1,1#cut, classic style) sits on the cut face of the half base at (1,1).
Handle at (0,0) top face (handle:0,0,0;top), chained over the cover at (0,0) and (1,0) top covers, so it spans the top of the organizer.

Fit is checked, not weight or strength. Build is 4 full bases plus a half base, 3 bins, 1 drawer, 1 handle, 2 covers and joint bolts; meshClash reads 'clear'. Portability is only implied by the handle and compact footprint; I did not verify weight or load.

finish.summary: Built a compact organizer: four hex base blocks and a half base, locked with joint bolts; three removable bins for small parts; one drawer on the half base's cut face; and a carry handle across the top covers. check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors or loose-body warnings (only an informational note that open faces could take caps). Fit is verified, not strength or weight.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
